rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with `name:` front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references`. The requirement's only obligation here is that each link to a file for specialized situations says when to read it.

The skill has no Markdown links. It points to other files only through code-span paths, and I treated each of those as a link.

- **`references/review-prompt.md`:** Workflow step 3 (Review) names it. It tells the main agent to have each review subagent read it, once per requirement group, while reviewing new or changed requirements. It adds a fallback: if subagents can't be started, the main agent reviews each group itself against that prompt. That says when to read it.
- **The habeas-evidence skill's `references/fixme.md`:** The closing paragraph of "Choosing references" names it with the condition "To defer a gap the user agrees to, use `{fixme}` as ... describes". That says when to read it.
- **Other pointers:** The habeas skill's `SKILL.md` (named in the intro and in step 3), the habeas-evidence "Rules" section, its "Uncovered Rust items" section, and "Disagreeing assessments" are each tied to a situation (writing directive syntax, a review subagent, committing changed text, uncovered items, disagreeing assessments). They are also not files inside this skill's own bundle.

No unconditional or condition-less link to a specialized file turned up, so I found no gap. No violation matches were listed.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
